description: Large dataset of oracle bone character images, deciphered and undeciphered
notes: Decoded + undecoded: 77,064 images / 1,588 deciphered, 62,989 images / 9,411 undeciphered. Has images: yes. License confirmed (read from the paper, 2026-10-03): CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial research reuse permitted, attribution required. Archive has 3 folders: deciphered, undeciphered, and a third explicitly marked by the authors as unreliable data from GuoXueDaShi — exclude or quarantine that third folder rather than ingesting it as-is. The author is reusing this for the oracle-bone dataset plan; fine for this hobby/research project (not commercializing).

description: Hand-crafted educational WeChat series explaining about 900 commonly readable oracle bone characters one by one: traced glyph image plus a secondary reference glyph, a 会意-style compositional gloss in prose (e.g. 家 = 宀 + 豕), and citations to 《甲骨文合集》 and 《新版殷墟甲骨文实用字典》 catalog numbers
notes: Personal WeChat 公众号 series by 太和山居, started 2020-01-12. Per the author's own intro: ~4,500 oracle bone characters catalogued to date, ~1,000+ considered readable, ~900 of those covered here (drawn mainly from 《甲骨文合集》, 《新版殷墟甲骨文实用字典》, 《甲骨文常用字字典》). Decoded only. Has images: yes, per character. Hand-crafted educational content, not a bulk corpus; article links collected locally in wechat-content.md since each character is its own WeChat post. Confirm reuse license before using beyond personal review. Good for spot-checking zx_char/zx_part decompositions against an independent source, and for seeding prose glosses for the semantic layer.

description: An open dataset for oracle bone character recognition and decipherment: 77,064 images / 1,588 deciphered + 62,989 images / 9,411 undeciphered signs
notes: Nature Scientific Data, 2024. Companion paper to the HUST-OBC git-repo row above. Image-only, no semantic network. License section (checked 2026-10-03): CC BY-NC 4.0. Local PDF: literatures/HUST-OBC-2401.15365v4.pdf.

description: Deciphering Oracle Bone Language with Diffusion Models: conditional diffusion model generates candidate modern-character glyphs from an oracle glyph
notes: ACL 2024 Best Paper. Purely visual/generative; no meaning graph. License checked 2026-10-03: code/data repo (github.com/guanhaisu/OBSD) has no LICENSE file and no license mentioned in its README -- default all-rights-reserved under copyright; would need to contact the authors before reusing code or any released data.

description: Deciphering Ancient Chinese Characters with Radical Reconstruction: decomposes oracle bone script into strokes/radicals, reconstructs the modern counterpart via Transformer
notes: ICDAR 2024. Introduces the ACCP dataset. Structural decomposition, not meaning. License checked 2026-10-03: code/data repo (github.com/Pengjie-W/Puzzle-Pieces-Picker) has no LICENSE file and no license mentioned in its README -- same all-rights-reserved caveat as OBSD; the ACCP dataset's own reuse terms are unstated.

description: Zero-shot Character Recognition via Radical-based Reasoning: radical identification plus reasoning over a Character Knowledge Graph
notes: IJCAI 2023. Introduces the OracleRC dataset. Graph of radical/structure relations, not curated meanings. Checked 2026-10-03: no public GitHub repo found for OracleRC -- it does not appear to be publicly released; likely available only on request to the authors, if at all.

description: Towards Unified Visual-Linguistic Understanding of Oracle Bone Scripts through Cross-Modal Knowledge Fusion: LLaVA-based LVLM plus graph-based semantic reasoning, new OracleSem dataset (1,762 annotated characters)
notes: 2024. Closest prior work to this project's plan, but its graph is built from annotating the 1,762 oracle characters themselves, not a pre-existing full-lexicon network. Read closely before claiming novelty. Checked 2026-10-03: no public GitHub repo found for OracleSem -- does not appear to be publicly released.

description: Oracle bone script decipherment via human-workflow-inspired deep learning: rubbing parsing, radical/diachronic morphological analysis, corpus-based semantic alignment, philological validation
notes: Accepted, The Innovation, 2026. "Semantic" here means corpus-usage alignment, not a decomposition-meaning graph. License checked 2026-10-03: code/framework (github.com/Yuliang-Liu/AlphaOracle) is Apache-2.0, permissive -- but the paper states it does NOT redistribute original rubbing images/scans for copyrighted sources, only derived resources (indices, metadata), citing fair use under PRC copyright law. The corpus itself (73,883 rubbings) is not reusable as images from this release.
